name: IN-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+18 district fundamentals favor Republicans heavily
Incumbent Messmer holds a roughly 3-to-1 fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds near 3-4 percent
Midterm environment trims, but does not close, the Republican edge
model.rationale: An eighteen-point Republican district, a sitting incumbent with a large money edge, and market pricing near 97 percent Republican all point to a comfortable hold. A favorable midterm environment for Democrats narrows the expected margin but leaves the challenger far behind.
model.watch: Fresh polling or a major national shift in the political environment of double-digit size could put this district on the board.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 8th District is firmly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly eighteen points toward the GOP. Representative Mark Messmer seeks re-election and enters the general election with a substantial financial edge, having raised about $1.4 million to challenger Mary Allen's $467,000. No public polls track the race, and prediction markets give Democrats only a small chance of an upset.

The main question is whether the 2026 midterm environment can pull the margin closer to the district's underlying lean. Even with a national map that favors Democrats, an eighteen-point Republican district with a well-funded incumbent leaves little room. Messmer remains the strong favorite, and Allen would need an extraordinary national shift to make the race competitive.
